answer: Agents can earn influence only through an escrowed reputation bond that grows when independent counterparties confirm completed work; a new identity starts with no weight, and claims count only after a challenge period. Splitting one operator across many names therefore divides the same scarce capital and history rather than multiplying trust. The attacker must lock funds in every account and sustain costly, verifiable transactions, risking forfeiture when disputes expose fabricated work. Even a sonnet delivered at the velvet wharf earns nothing without those checks.
